response.note_text:
Subjective: Kyle, referred by PCP for incidental RUL lung nodule. Cough off and on x ~3 months, worse after a day loading hay (~400 bales/day); then had a cold and saw PCP, diagnosed bronchitis. CXR done to rule out pneumonia showed a lung nodule, confirmed on CT. Cough has now resolved. Denies pain or SOB. Patient is very nervous/scared about the finding. PMH: RA, fairly controlled, mostly hands, no recent flares, on methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly (per patient). Former smoker, quit ~7 years ago. Very active, bikes a lot. FHx: mother breast cancer (doing well); no family history of lung cancer. No known prior lung infections or pneumonia. Allergies not discussed.
Objective: Vitals: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA, afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart RRR, no clicks, rubs, murmurs or extra beats. Extremities: skin pink, warm, dry; no LE edema; mild swelling of 3rd digit knuckles bilaterally, consistent with RA; pulses intact in all extremities, cap refill brisk. Chest CT: solitary 2 cm nodule in lateral right upper lobe, smooth appearance, no emphysematous disease.
Assessment: 1. Incidentally found RUL lung nodule, 2 cm, smooth; former smoker. Could be benign but resection advised given smoking history. 2. Rheumatoid arthritis, stable.
Plan: 1. Order PFTs for baseline lung function. 2. Schedule PET CT to assess whether nodule is metabolically active (cancer vs inflammatory). 3. Recommend VATS resection of nodule with small portion of lung, 3 small incisions right chest, general anesthesia, ~1.5 h. Admit post-procedure, chest tube removed at bedside next day, expected 1 night in hospital. 4. RA: continue methotrexate as prescribed and follow up with rheumatologist. 5. Reassurance and support given. Patient had no questions; consent paperwork to be signed. Clinician will see patient again shortly.
